back_translation: When King Hezekiah heard that report, he tore his royal robes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the royal scribe, and the senior priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz,
to say to Isaiah: "Hezekiah says this: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace — like children come to the point of birth with no strength to deliver them.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master sent to revile the living God, and will rebuke him for the words the LORD your God has heard. Therefore pray for the remnant that still survives."
When the officials of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,
Isaiah answered, "Tell your master: the LORD says this: 'Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have reviled Me.
Behold, I will put a spirit in him; he will hear a rumor and return to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"
When the Rabshakeh heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he withdrew and found the king fighting against Libnah.
Now Sennacherib received a report about Tirhakah king of Cush: "He has set out to fight against you." When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying:
"Tell Hezekiah king of Judah: 'Do not let the God you trust deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not fall into the hand of the king of Assyria.
Behold, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands — destroying them completely. Will you then escape?
Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed deliver them — Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, of Arpad, of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?'"
Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD, saying:
"O LORD of Hosts, God of Israel, who sits enthroned above the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
O LORD, incline Your ear and hear; O LORD, open Your eyes and see. Hear all the words of Sennacherib, who has sent men to revile the living God.
O LORD, it is true that the kings of Assyria have destroyed all these lands and their territories,
and have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them — for they were not gods, but only wood and stone, the work of human hands.
Now, O LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone are the LORD."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "The LORD, the God of Israel, says this: Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word the LORD has spoken against him: 'The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you.
Whom have you taunted and reviled? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your servants you have taunted the Lord. You have said: 'With my many chariots I have ascended the high mountains, the utmost depths of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, its finest cypresses. I have reached its farthest summit, its most luxuriant forest.
I have dug wells and drunk water; with the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.'
Have you not heard? I ordained this long ago; I planned it in days of old. Now I have brought it to pass — that you should crush fortified cities into heaps of rubble.
Therefore their inhabitants were drained of strength, dismayed and ashamed. They were like plants of the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched by the sun before it can grow.
But I know everything — your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.
Because your raging and your arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bridle in your mouth, and I will turn you back by the way you came.'

This will be the sign for you, O Hezekiah: this year you will eat what grows by itself, in the second year what springs from that, but in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
For a remnant will go out from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.
Therefore the LORD says this about the king of Assyria: 'He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
He will return by the way he came, and he will not enter this city,' the LORD has declared.
'I will protect this city and save it, for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.'"
Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down one hundred eighty-five thousand men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people rose in the morning, there were corpses strewn everywhere.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria withdrew his army, departed, and returned to dwell at Nineveh.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon reigned in his place.
